title: Effective Capacity of CFTR Met470: What the Direction of Disease Association Can Supply Where Protein Measurement Is Silent
content: Background: The CFTR M470V polymorphism (rs213950, c.1408A>G) is the most common coding variant in CFTR. What matters physiologically is the allele's effective capacity: the chloride transport delivered by protein that has matured, reached the membrane and is working there. The two components dominating it, the steady-state mature pool and membrane residence time, have never been measured for the two alleles; the two that have point in opposite directions on scales that cannot be combined. Methods: We recomputed every published M470V association under a homozygote-contrast model from the original genotype counts, classified each phenotype as supply-limited or not before examining effect estimates, and characterised the linkage context of rs213950. The direction of association was then read as an independent indicator of effective capacity, on the stated premise that risk in supply-limited phenotypes reflects insufficient delivered CFTR. Results: Across nine supply-limited cohorts spanning two ancestries and three diseases, every odds ratio exceeded unity (9/9; sign test P = 0.002 by cohort, 3/3 and P = 0.125 by disease) with no significant heterogeneity (I2 = 39%, P = 0.11). Estimates were indistinguishable between Europeans and East Asians (1.34 vs 1.65, P = 0.35) although the two differ more than twofold in linkage-block size and carry Met470 on tract backgrounds of opposite quality. In the one phenotype that is not supply-limited the direction reversed (lung cancer, OR 0.65, P = 0.007), on a single study. Conclusions: Linkage-driven association predicts heterogeneity across populations with different haplotype structure; the data show homogeneity, localising the effect to the shared element, residue 470 itself. That effect is negative for effective capacity, and the single reversal suggests it is phenotype-specific rather than globally deleterious. The decisive experiment is a direct comparison of steady-state mature CFTR and membrane residence between the alleles under identical conditions.
